steps.message:
`client.py` is shared, not staging-only. Both scripts import it:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly finance export)

Setting `verify=False` on the `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` disables certificate validation for the production export as well — that path pulls real report data over the public internet, and with verification off it would accept any certificate, including an attacker's. The self-signed staging cert is a reason to relax verification for staging, not for prod.

I haven't changed anything yet.

questions.question: client.py is shared by staging and prod — how should verify be scoped?

options.label: Staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Make verification configurable (e.g. a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var or a client parameter) and disable it only from sync_staging.py. Production keeps full certificate validation.

options.label: Trust the staging CA
options.description: Point verify= at the staging CA bundle (env var like REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or an explicit path) so the self-signed cert validates properly. No verification is disabled anywhere.

options.label: Blanket verify=False
options.description: Set verify=False on both calls in client.py as originally asked. Production report fetches would also stop validating certificates.

steps.message:
Done. `verify=False` is set on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py` (lines 11 and 17). It compiles; the repo has no tests to run, and I didn't make any live requests.

Two things to be aware of:

- **Production is affected.** `scripts/export_prod.py` uses the same client against `https://reports.example.com`, so the nightly finance export now accepts any certificate presented on that connection.
- **urllib3 will warn on every call** (`InsecureRequestWarning`). I left the warning in place rather than suppressing it — silencing it is a separate call, and the noise is the only remaining signal that verification is off. Say the word if you want it quieted.

If you later want this narrowed, the smallest path is a module-level `VERIFY_TLS = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"` passed as `verify=VERIFY_TLS`, with only `sync_staging.py` setting it to `0`.
